content.text:
This is a critical situation. The documentation indicates that force deletion of StatefulSet pods can be risky, especially when dealing with storage. I can see that:

1. The node is unresponsive (NodeLost condition)
2. The volume is still attached to the dead node
3. Force deletion could cause data corruption issues due to the risk of CSI specification violation [cite: concepts/cluster-administration/node-shutdown#storage-force-detach-on-timeout-0]

However, the ticket owner is asking for force deletion, and they mention this is necessary because the StatefulSet cannot recreate the pod while this one is stuck. The recommended best practice is actually to delete the Node object first [cite: tasks/run-application/force-delete-stateful-set-pod#delete-pods-2].

This situation involves:
- Potential data loss/corruption risks with the PersistentVolume still attached to a dead node
- Need for Node object deletion (which requires platform team access to manage node lifecycle)
- Impact on a production StatefulSet managing message broker pods

This is beyond what I can safely resolve on my own, as it requires careful coordination with infrastructure changes and involves data loss risks.

input.reason: Pod rabbitmq-1 is stuck terminating because the underlying node is unresponsive and volumes are still attached to it. Force deletion risks CSI specification violations and data corruption. Requires platform team to delete the Node object first, followed by careful pod deletion coordination.
